title: CLCON/205/2007 of M/S SOCIAL LEASING INDIALTD Vs PRINCIPAL SECRETARY FINANCE GOVT. OF U.P.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
CLCON No.205 of 2007
M/s Social Leasing (India) Ltd.
 ÖPetitioner
Versus
Shekar Agarwal, Principal Secretary (Finance),
Govt. of U.P., & Anr.
 ÖRespondents
Sri S.K. Posti, Advocate for the applicant
Smt. Beena Pandey, Standing Counsel for the State of U.P.
Honíble Tarun Agarwala, J.
The writ court passed the following order:-
ìBy means of this writ petition, the petitioners
have prayed for writ of mandamus directing the
respondents to fulfill their commitment as
guaranteed by State Government through Chief
Secretary, Finance which is contained in annexure
no.2 to the writ petition.
2. The basis of the relief sought is on the
ground that the Managing Director of respondent
no.1 has stated in his initiation letter that 90% of the
shares of Respondent No.1 are held by State
Government and even the Chief Secretary, Finance
also gave the guarantee of the repayment of the
principle amount and the interest accrued on it.

2
3. A counter affidavit has been filed by the
State of U.P./Respondent No.2 in which the liability
has not been denied but the State of U.P. has come
forward with a case that since the
company/respondent no.1 is under liquidation, the
petitionerís investment is secure and the same shall
be paid to him after the sale of property under the
orders of Bombay High Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner
submitted that the major part of the property in
dispute has been sold and the petitioner has not
been paid a single penny, therefore, it was the
liability of the Principal Secretary, Finance, State of
U.P. to have ensured the payment of petitionerís
investment with interest in the company at the first
instance after the Government debts and payment of
wages to the employees. Therefore, the Principle
Secretary (Finance) State of U.P. is directed to ensure
that the payment to the petitioner is made for his
investment alongwith interest by making an
application before the Liquidator for payment of the
investment made by the petitioner with interest as
per the guarantee/commitment given by the State
Government. The petitioner shall also make an
application to the liquidator annexing therewith the
copy of the application made by the Secretary,
Finance, State of U.P.
5. With the aforesaid observation, the petition
is disposed of finally.î

3
Since the order of the writ court was not
complied with the present contempt application
was filed.
During the pendency of the contempt
proceedings, the opposite party has paid a sum of
Rs.3.00 Lakhs to the applicant which is also
recorded in the order of the Court dated
16.12.2011. The applicant, not being satisfied,
contends that full amount has not been given and
that the opposite party is still required to pay the
balance amount along with interest.
The contempt proceedings cannot be used as a
tool to recover the money in a commercial
transaction. The contempt proceedings can be
initiated when there is willful disobedience or non-compliance of the order of the writ court. In the
present case, the Court finds that the respondentsí
Company is under liquidation and a Liquidator has
been appointed. The writ court directed the parties
to file an appropriate application before the
Liquidator from where the payment of the
investment made by the applicant would be
cleared. Nothing has been brought on record to
indicate that such compliance of the order was
made or not made by the opposite party or by the
applicant himself. In any case, recovery of money
can be done under the Companyís Act, or in
alternative, if the applicant is not satisfied with
whatever payment has been made by the opposite

4
party, it is open to the applicant to file a suit for
recovery of the money. The contempt court is not
an appropriate forum. Consequently, the notices
are discharged and the contempt application is
dismissed.
